Subject: RE: Spike -> 5xx/429s affecting checkout (examples attached)

Summary of triage (observed 07:38-08:15 PST):

- Root trigger: an internal control-plane job incorrectly marked a small set of edge nodes as degraded (health check flapping) while an unrelated deployment was in progress. The routing layer took nodes OOS and routed traffic to fewer nodes.
- Amplification: client retries from multiple tenants hit the reduced capacity; concurrent prefix-KV cache invalidations forced longer token-latency on cold hot-paths.
- Autoscale lag: our autoscaler threshold required sustained CPU/mem for 60s before adding capacity; during sharp fan-out the duration threshold prevented fast scaling and produced 429s.
- Alerting gap: we did not have an alert for 'rapid node OOS rate' — only absolute capacity and per-node health symptoms.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Re-enabled healthy nodes by reverting the control-plane flag at 08:01 PST.
- Temporarily relaxed autoscale duration threshold to 10s and added short-term burst capacity.
- Deployed a hotfix to reduce KV cache invalidation TTLs to prevent cold-path latency spikes.

Next actions (short term):
- Create an alert for node OOS rate > 5 in 1m (owner: infra-sre).
- Add a circuit-breaker to limit tenant retry fan-out at gateway, with token-bucket backpressure (owner: serving-runtime).
- Review autoscaler policy; move to an aggressive fast-path for short spikes (owner: infra).

I'll follow up with a compact postmortem by Monday and a runbook update.

— Dev
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: SwiftPay incident: summary and near-term commitments

Hi Daniel — thank you again for the quick logs and traces. Below is a concise summary we will share with your execs; happy to tailor further for your stakeholders.

Incident summary:
- What happened: A subset of routing-edge nodes were marked degraded during a control-plane update, reducing available capacity. Client retries amplified the reduced capacity, causing elevated 5xx/429 rates between 07:38-08:02 PST on 2026-11-14.
- Impact: SwiftPay experienced increased checkout failures (~4% payment drop) during the window.
- Root causes: 1) control-plane health-flapping and incorrect node OOS marking; 2) autoscaler duration thresholds too conservative for sub-minute spikes; 3) missing alert for rapid node OOS rate; 4) no gateway-level tenant retry circuit-breaker.

Near-term commitments (timeline):
- Done (within hours): reverted node state, relaxed autoscale duration to 10s, temporary burst capacity (completed 2026-11-14).
- 48h: full incident timeline and written postmortem (owner: Soojin Lee).
- 5 business days: deploy gateway tenant circuit-breaker and alert for node OOS rate (owners: serving-runtime, infra-sre).
- 10 business days: autoscaler fast-path policy and runbook updates + SLO clarification for transient bursts (owners: infra, product ops).

Attachments: error-sample.log, autoscale-metrics.png.

Ask: please confirm if the 5-day remediation window works for SwiftPay and whether you want an on-call exec update tomorrow at 10am PST.

Regards,
Sooj

Subject: FINAL: SwiftPay postmortem + action tracker (INC-54931)

Team — final postmortem and actions for INC-54931 attached. High-level takeaways and owners below for exec review.

Key findings:
- Control-plane incident: a deploy induced transient health-check failures that marked 6 edge nodes OOS. Change rolled out without a pre-check that would have caught the flapping pattern.
- Autoscaler tuning: the 60s sustained-window failed to account for rapid tenant-driven bursts; we now have a fast-path to provision burst capacity in 10s.
- Retry amplification: tenant clients with immediate retry loops significantly increased concurrency pressure; no gateway circuit-breaker existed to cap tenant fan-out.
- Observability gap: no alert for 'node OOS rate' and per-tenant request-surge alarms were coarse.

Action tracker (owners & ETA):
- INF-7241: Add node OOS rate alert (owner: infra-sre) — ETA 2d.
- INF-7242: Gateway tenant circuit-breaker rollout + integration tests (owner: serving-runtime) — ETA 5d.
- INF-7243: Autoscaler fast-path policy & config (owner: infra) — ETA 10d.
- INF-7244: Runbook update + tabletop walkthrough (owner: platform-ops) — ETA 5d.
- INF-7245: Customer-facing exec note & SLO review meeting (owner: account-team) — ETA 3d.

Customer communication: Soojin will send a formal exec note to SwiftPay (sent 2026-11-16); we'll offer a post-incident review call and provide runbook access.

Attachments: postmortem-action-tracker.csv. Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7241. PagerDuty incident INC-54931.
